text:
Mark Jankowski is 32 and scoring at a pace he has never come close to. He has 8 goals in 15 games for Carolina, six in his last ten, with his ice time up 2:19 a night. The New York Times framed it as stepping up for Jordan Staal with "Conn Smythe shoes to fill," and NHL.com says he has "taken advantage" of a big opportunity.

The chances are real. He has 4.5 expected goals on his own shots over the last ten games against 2.7 usual (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and his rate of 1.36 per 60 is well above last season's 0.90. The bad news is the finish: 8 goals on 5.0 expected, a 29% shooting rate against 17% last season. That will come down.

What stays is the defensive side. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 92nd percentile at taking chances away last season, and noted his chances ran ahead of his goals then. Flames Nation called him a reminder that development sometimes takes time, fair for the highest-drafted Canadian high school player ever. Our projection has him around 23 goals, which would be a career year.
headline: Jankowski is filling a big hole, and filling the net
